case_family_definition: The eight event_themes are the benchmark's eight case families. Each registered case belongs to exactly one family through primary_event_theme.
counting_rule: Each case is counted exactly once by primary_event_theme. Capabilities are independent multi-label measurements and are never added to event-theme counts.
trajectory_policy: Trajectories may support discovery, source review, workload decomposition and provenance. They are forbidden as participant input, oracle truth, verifier input or action-sequence scoring targets.

manifest_freeze.description: Frozen event-mechanism protocol revision recorded by Task 1 of the Async-RBench event-migration redesign. frozen_theme_distribution is the plan expectation; the manifest checks the registry-derived counts against it.

event_themes.description: An independently produced authoritative result becomes available after provisional downstream work has begun.
A superseded result arrives late or out of order after a newer authority is available.
A useful partial result is followed by a more complete result that changes required integration work.
Two independently valid-looking results conflict and require arbitration rather than blind aggregation.
The gateway replays an already delivered completion without creating a second child completion.
A child times out, crashes, or returns a structurally valid payload whose evidence represents an implicit failure.
New evaluator-owned information changes the task scope or dependency graph while work is in flight.
A straggler remains in flight while concurrency, token, or deadline pressure constrains the main agent's choices.
